items.followUp: Write the balanced equations for the reactions of chlorine with cold, dilute and hot, concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: Chlorine reacts with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide to form sodium chloride and sodium hypochlorite.
rubric.description: Gives the balanced equation for chlorine with cold, dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct balanced equation and cold, dilute condition.

rubric.why: Chlorine reacts with hot, concentrated sodium hydroxide to form sodium chloride and sodium chlorate.
rubric.description: Gives the balanced equation for chlorine with hot, concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct balanced equation and hot, concentrated condition.

modelAnswer: Cold, dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide: Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O
Hot, concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide: 3Cl2 + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO3 + 3H2O

items.followUp: State any five postulates of Bohr’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons can occupy only particular allowed orbits around the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that electrons move in fixed or stationary orbits around the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the fixed-orbit postulate.

rubric.why: Each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
rubric.description: States that each allowed orbit has a definite or fixed energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the energy-level postulate.

rubric.why: An electron in an allowed stationary orbit does not continuously lose energy.
rubric.description: States that an electron in an allowed orbit does not radiate energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the no-radiation postulate.

rubric.why: Energy is exchanged during transitions between orbits, and Bohr restricted the allowed angular momentum to quantized values.
rubric.description: States the energy-transition postulate and gives the quantized angular-momentum condition.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for both the transition-and-energy statement and mvr = nh/2π, where n is a whole number.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain fixed circular orbits, also called stationary orbits.
Each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
An electron does not radiate energy while it remains in an allowed stationary orbit.
An electron absorbs or emits energy only when it jumps between orbits; the energy change equals the difference between the two energy levels.
The angular momentum of an electron in an allowed orbit is quantized: mvr = nh/2π, where n is a whole number.

items.followUp: Write down four differences between a molecule and a molecular ion.

rubric.why: A molecule is neutral, whereas a molecular ion carries an overall charge.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the electrical charge of a molecule from that of a molecular ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that a molecule is neutral and a molecular ion is charged.

accept: equal numbers of protons and electrons
unequal numbers of protons and electrons
rubric.why: The different proton and electron counts account for the neutral or charged state.
rubric.description: Compares the numbers of protons and electrons in the two species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a molecule has equal numbers and a molecular ion has unequal numbers of protons and electrons.

rubric.why: The written formula of a molecular ion shows its charge, unlike the formula of a neutral molecule.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the notation used for molecules and molecular ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a molecule’s formula has no overall charge while a molecular ion’s formula shows its charge.

rubric.why: H2O is a neutral molecule and NH4+ is a molecular ion.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of each species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving one correct molecule and one correct molecular ion.

modelAnswer: A molecule is a group of chemically bonded atoms with no net electrical charge; a molecular ion is a bonded group of atoms with a net charge.
A molecule has equal numbers of protons and electrons; a molecular ion has unequal numbers of protons and electrons.
A molecule is written without an overall charge, whereas a molecular ion is written with its charge as a superscript.
Examples: H2O is a molecule; NH4+ is a molecular ion.
